Running a league or a tournament from your phone: schedule, table and bracket

24 November 2026 · Kadar

Every summer someone at the club gets the job of running the tournament: eight teams, one pitch, a sheet of paper on the clubhouse door and a pen that has gone missing. By the semi-finals nobody is sure who plays whom. A phone does this job better than the paper.

Pick the format that fits the day

  • League: everyone plays everyone, once or twice. Fair, but needs time: six teams playing once is fifteen matches.
  • Knockout cup: lose and you are out. Quick, and every match matters, but half the teams go home after one game.
  • Groups, then knockout: the usual choice for a one-day tournament. Everyone gets at least two or three matches, and the day still ends with a final.

Let the schedule write itself

In Kadar you type in the teams, pick one of the three formats and the schedule is made for you: rounds for a league, the bracket for a cup, free passes where the number of teams is uneven. You add the time and the pitch to each match.

Keep the table right

The table is where arguments start. Enter each result once and the table is recalculated: three points for a win, one for a draw, then goal difference, goals scored and the match between the two teams. In a cup the winner moves to the next round by itself, and a draw asks for the penalty shoot-out result.

Show it to everyone

Parents on the touchline and players waiting for their match ask the same question all day: who is next, and where do we stand?

  • Share the table or the bracket as a picture to the tournament group after every round.
  • If you stream a match from the schedule, the teams and the round are already filled in, and the result lands in the table when you end the match.
  • Show the table, the bracket, the round's matches or the top scorers as a full-picture graphic on the stream during a break.

What to know before you start

A competition in Kadar is stored on the phone that created it. Two phones on two pitches do not share one table yet, so one person keeps the results and the others send the scores to them. Leagues and cups with their graphics are part of PRO, and everything in PRO is free until 28 February 2027.

Try it at your next match
